ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is assembled from a pair of set squares. What is the degree measure of $\angle ABC$ in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle F=30^\circ$ and $\angle EAC=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABF=\angle EAC-\angle F=45^\circ-30^\circ=15^\circ$, \\
$\because$ $\angle FBC=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC=\angle FBC-\angle ABF=90^\circ-15^\circ=\boxed{75^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram first: F, A, C, D lie on the same horizontal base; DE is vertical; B is where the slanted 30° edge from F and the slanted 45° edge from A/E meet; BC is the other leg of the right set square and is perpendicular to BF. From the text, use that the figure is made of set squares, so the visible 30° and 45° markings are standard set-square angles and the corner at B of triangle FBC is a right angle. Treat the horizontal base as direction 0°. Then BF has direction 30° above the base, while AB/AE has direction 45° above the base. Thus the small angle between BA and BF at B is 45° - 30° = 15°. Since BF is perpendicular to BC, ∠FBC = 90°, so ∠ABC = 90° - 15° = 75°.
